topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining how known immune cells and molecules combine to initiate and resolve inflammatory reactions.

topics.label: Innate recognition of infection and cellular damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system senses pathogens and tissue injury using molecular patterns and specialized pattern recognition receptor systems.

topics.label: Inflammatory response execution and systemic consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how innate activation triggers sentinel cell signaling, leukocyte extravasation into tissues, lymphatic transport, and systemic complications such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the mechanisms required to terminate acute inflammation, rebuild damaged tissue, and manage unresolved or chronic inflammatory conditions.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the subject of the next lecture.
